info.name: FoC User Service
info.description:
Every route of the User Service, ordered so the whole collection runs top to bottom in the Collection Runner with no manual step: the OTPs are read out of Mailpit's HTTP API by a pre-request script.

Needs the compose stack up (`docker compose up`) - the service on baseUrl and Mailpit on mailpitUrl.

Each address gets three OTP requests per ten minutes, shared across register, resend and forgot - so every folder here owns its own address and spends that budget deliberately. Every address is generated fresh per run, so the runner is safe to press repeatedly.

The exception is the two '(manual OTP)' folders at the end - the admin user/role lifecycle and the OTP-protected self-service profile changes. They still need an ADMIN accessToken, targetUserId and each OTP pasted by hand. Exclude them from the runner.

AI Assistance Disclosure: Tool: Claude Code (model: Claude Opus 5), date: 2026-09-28. Scope: generated the requests, the assertions and the Mailpit OTP lookup. Author review: the full collection run green against the compose stack.

AI Assistance Disclosure (the manual folders): Tool: Claude Code (model: Claude Opus 5), date: 2026-09-26. Scope: generated the collection for the three sign-up routes. 2026-09-28 (model: Claude Sonnet 5): added List users (admin) and Change role (admin) (Step 10 - these routes were marked Postman-verified in admin.controller.ts/admin.service.ts, but the requests used for that were never saved into this collection), the six Step 12 requests (Request OTP through Deactivate account), and Reactivate user (admin) (Step 13). Author review: the six Step 12 requests were exercised via Postman against the compose stack on 2026-09-28 (all endpoints, including the retry-with-the-same-code behaviour on Change email - request and Change password) - see /ai/usage-log.md. Reactivate user (admin) was exercised the same way on 2026-09-28 (deactivate then reactivate, 404 for an unknown id, 409 NOT_DEACTIVATED for an already-ACTIVE target). List users (admin) and Change role (admin) (Step 10) are still unverified through this file specifically, even though the routes themselves were separately confirmed working via ad hoc Postman requests when Step 10 was built.

request.description: 401. One failure out of the five that would lock the address - harmless on its own.

Only @u.nus.edu and @nus.edu.sg may hold an account. Subdomains are not accepted either: evil.u.nus.edu is a domain we do not control, so the match is exact. Validation runs in a pipe, before the service, so a 400 never touches the rate limiter - which is why the fixed addresses in this folder are safe to reuse every run.

At least 8 characters with a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter and a digit. The ceiling is 72 bytes, because that is all bcrypt reads - two passwords sharing a 72-byte prefix would otherwise verify against the same hash.

request.description: +65 is a real prefix and 12345678 is eight digits, but together they are not a valid Singapore number. libphonenumber knows each country's numbering plan; a regex cannot.
Every body is strict, so an unknown field is a 400 and never silently dropped. That is what stops a caller smuggling a role into a sign-up.

OTP_EXPIRED, deliberately not 404. A wrong code, a stale code and no sign-up at all answer identically - otherwise submitting 000000 against any address would read 404 as "not registering" and 400 as "registering right now", which discloses who is signing up without ever guessing a code.

item.name: Profile (manual OTP)
item.description: Not yet part of the automated run - exclude this folder in the Collection Runner. Paste each OTP from Mailpit into the otp variable by hand.

request.description: 200 with the self profile: userId, displayName, email, countryCode, mobileNumber - no role, status or createdAt (that's the admin-facing shape returned by GET /admin/users instead). 401 with no token.

200 with the updated self profile. No OTP needed - displayName is the one profile field that isn't OTP-protected. Any field other than displayName (e.g. role, email) is rejected with 400, since the body schema is strict.

202 with { otpExpiresAt }. purpose is one of EMAIL_CHANGE, MOBILE_CHANGE, PASSWORD_CHANGE, DEACTIVATION - swap the value above for whichever flow you're testing next. Always mails the code to the CURRENT email, even for MOBILE_CHANGE (every OTP in this service goes out by email). For DEACTIVATION, 409 LAST_ADMIN before any code is issued if the caller is the sole active admin. 429 after three requests in ten minutes.

202 with { otpExpiresAt }. Run 'Request OTP' with purpose EMAIL_CHANGE first and paste that code (from the CURRENT address's inbox) into otp here. On success, mails a SECOND code to newEmail - paste that one into otp before 'Change email - verify'. 409 EMAIL_TAKEN if newEmail already belongs to another account (the first code is still consumed even then). OTP errors otherwise.

200 with the refreshed self profile - email is now newEmail. Uses the SECOND code, mailed to newEmail by 'Change email - request', not the first one. 409 EMAIL_TAKEN if newEmail was claimed by someone else in the meantime. No refresh tokens are revoked - existing sessions stay logged in.

200 with the refreshed self profile. Run 'Request OTP' with purpose MOBILE_CHANGE first. countryCode and mobileNumber must be a valid pair together (libphonenumber-js), not just individually well-formed. OTP errors otherwise; 400 for an invalid number.

204, no tokens back. Run 'Request OTP' with purpose PASSWORD_CHANGE first. Revokes every refresh token, so this session's accessToken still works (up to 15 min) but refreshToken no longer does - log in again to get a fresh pair. 400 VALIDATION_ERROR if newPassword matches the current one (still costs you the code). OTP errors otherwise.

204. Run 'Request OTP' with purpose DEACTIVATION first. Sets status DEACTIVATED and revokes every refresh token; logging in afterward gives 403 ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED. 409 LAST_ADMIN if the caller is the sole active admin - promote another admin via 'Change role (admin)' first to test the success path instead. An admin can undo this with 'Reactivate user (admin)'.

item.name: Admin (manual OTP)
item.description: Not yet part of the automated run - exclude this folder in the Collection Runner. accessToken must belong to an ADMIN, and targetUserId must be set by hand.

request.description: 200 with { items }, each in the admin-facing Profile shape (adds role/status/createdAt over the self profile). role and status are both optional exact-match filters - remove or disable either query param to drop it. 403 for a non-admin caller (logged as UNAUTHORISED_ACCESS); 401 with no token. accessToken must belong to an ADMIN.

200 with the target's admin-facing profile. role is 'USER' or 'ADMIN'. 404 if targetUserId doesn't exist; 409 USER_NOT_ACTIVE if the target isn't ACTIVE; 409 CANNOT_MODIFY_SELF if targetUserId equals the caller's own id and role is USER (use 'Deactivate account' to remove your own admin access instead); 409 LAST_ADMIN if the caller is the sole active admin demoting themselves. 403/401 as above.

200 with the target's admin-facing profile, status ACTIVE. No body. 404 if targetUserId doesn't exist; 409 NOT_DEACTIVATED unless the target is currently DEACTIVATED (run 'Deactivate account' as that user first to test the success path). 403/401 as above.
